chunks: Muhammad ibn ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Za'lan, from Abu Ishaq al-Khurasani, from Amr ibn Jumi' al-Abdi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Our Shia are the pale, the withered, the slender, those who, when night covers them, welcome it with grief.

key_terms.الذَّابِلُونَ: The withered (showing signs of aging or devotion)
key_terms.الشَّاحِبُونَ: The pale (indicating asceticism or lack of sleep for worship)
key_terms.النَّاحِلُونَ: The slender (emaciated from fasting or worship)

ai.seo_question: What are the physical and spiritual signs of the true Shia according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, the 'pale and withered' appearance of the Shia is interpreted not as illness but as the physical manifestation of intense spiritual vigilance (Muraqabah) and deep contemplation (Tafakkur) regarding the Hereafter. This hadith, found in Al-Kafi, emphasizes that their solemnity at night reflects a conscious awareness of the transient nature of worldly life and the imminence of divine judgment, distinguishing them through their emotional and physical detachment from worldly comforts.
